description.narrative:
Somalia continues to face a severe and protracted drought crisis driven by consecutive poor rainy seasons, prolonged dry conditions, and rising temperatures. These climate shocks have significantly reduced water availability, weakened livestock, diminished agricultural production, and increased food insecurity across many regions. I
n Baki District of Awdal Region, Somaliland, drought conditions have severely affected agro-pastoral communities, resulting in declining household incomes, reduced milk production, loss of productive assets, and increased reliance on negative coping mechanisms such as reducing meal consumption, taking on debt, selling livestock, and migrating in search of water and pasture.To address these urgent humanitarian needs, the project will provide emergency cash assistance to 470 vulnerable households, benefiting approximately 2,820 individuals across four drought-affected villages: Old Baki, Kaxda, Baysare, and Qardhile. The intervention will prioritize households facing the highest levels of vulnerability, including female-headed households, internally displaced persons (IDPs), households with young children, pregnant and lactating women, elderly people, persons with disabilities, and families with limited livelihood opportunities.
The project will deliver three rounds of cash-for-food assistance through secure mobile money platforms, enabling affected households to purchase food according to their immediate needs and preferences. This approach will help improve household food consumption, prevent further deterioration of nutritional status, and reduce reliance on harmful coping strategies. By providing flexible cash support, the project will also contribute tosustaining local markets and preserving household dignity duringthe crisis.Community engagement and accountability will be central to implementation. The project will work closely with district authorities, community leaders, and representative community committees to ensure transparent beneficiary selection, effective targeting, and inclusive decision-making. Community feedback and complaints mechanisms will be established to strengthen accountability and ensure that concerns are addressed promptly throughout the projectcycle.In addition to addressing immediate food security needs, the intervention will contribute to strengthening household resilience against future climate shocks. By enabling families to protect productive assets, avoid distress livestock sales, and maintain essential livelihood resources, the project will help communities recover more quickly and reduce their vulnerability to future droughts.
The project will further promote gender equality, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, and environmental protection through targeted support, inclusive participation, and community-based approaches that foster social cohesion and local ownership.Through this integrated emergency response, the project aims to save lives, protect livelihoods, and support the recovery and resilience of drought-affected communities in Baki District, while contributing to broader efforts to address the growing humanitarian impacts of climate change in Somaliland.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
